description: "Supported through a USD 900,000 (KES 116.6 million) Loan Portfolio Guarantee Facility, with a maximum portfolio value of USD 1.8 million (KES 233.1 million), the facility targets four key segments of Kenya's digital economy: FinTech companies, Digital Credit Providers, e-commerce and digitally enabled MSMEs, and Digital Innovation Hubs and ecosystem enablers." title: ATK Debt II — Atlas Tower Kenya mobile tower expansion
description:
The proposed transaction is a multi-currency senior debt financing of up to US$30 million, including an IFC A Loan of up to US$20 million and remaining to be mobilized from a B Lender/parallel lender for Atlas Tower Kenya (ATK or the Company), an IFC client since 2021. The funding will (i) enable ATK to build and operate new macro towers in Kenya, expanding its existing portfolio of 442 towers; (ii) support ATK's Green Power Program which involves the large-scale deployment of solar power, battery storage, and off-grid or hybrid energy solutions to help reduce dependence on grid electricity and diesel; and (iii) refinance existing indebtedness (Project). ATK is an independent telecommunications infrastructure company operating in Kenya under a build-to-suit (BTS) model. Established in 2018, ATK owns and operates a portfolio of 442 towers and manages the full tower lifecycle, including site identification, land leasing, permitting, construction, energy solutions, and operations and maintenance.

The most significant expected project-level outcome is to increase the capacity of mobile networks in Kenya, resulting in improved access to quality connectivity for individuals and businesses. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will deepen the competitiveness of the mobile tower market in Kenya by expanding shared infrastructure integrating green power solutions via competition channels.

"A significant portion of the broader EU support package includes €37 million allocated to the Blue Raman submarine cable project," linking Djibouti, Somalia, Kenya and Tanzania to enhance regional internet capacity.

recipient: Government of Kenya, Ministry of Health
title: U.S. Department of State — Kenya health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy Cooperation Framework, 2025
description:
Paragraph 2.5.9.1 of the *Cooperation Framework between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Kenya on Health*: "The U.S. Government intends to provide $175,000,000 over the course of the Framework to support data systems. The Government of Kenya intends to continue investing in the Digital Superhighway."

Appendix 1 gives the annual split of the data-systems line: **US$30,000,000 (2026), US$75,000,000 (2027), US$50,000,000 (2028), US$10,000,000 (2029), US$10,000,000 (2030)** — US fiscal years, 15 October to 30 September.

Paragraph 2.5.9.2–2.5.9.3 states the named uses: Kenya's **TaifaCare HMIS** enhancement including laboratory and pharmacy integration and scale-up and the onboarding of standalone systems; the **National Logistics Management System (NLMIS)** including its pharmacy module, track-and-trace and health commodity inventory management; **Kenya's surveillance systems including EOC digitization** and the outbreak response data system; one comprehensive **Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)**; **KEMSA iLMIS and GS1 implementation**; and **Kenya's national and county data banks as its national and county health data warehouse**. Paragraph 2.5.9.4 records that the amount covers developers, product managers and systems engineers, cloud computing capacity and software licences, and hardware. Paragraph 2.5.9.5 leaves ongoing licensing, cloud, and hardware maintenance and replacement costs not specifically paid by the US Government to Kenya.

title: Nairobi Intelligent Transport System (ITS) Project

title: Mzalendo Trust — digital literacy, online safety and technology-facilitated GBV, Kenya
description: The project seeks to enhance the capacity of youth, women, and people with disabilities living in informal settlements on digital literacy and safety, and to enable civic education and awareness raising on Technology-Facilitated Gender Based Violence (TFGBV) through digital civic spaces. A growing area of concern in Kenya, TFGBV has far-reaching impacts on the rights, safety, and participation of individuals in digital and offline spaces, particularly women and girls. The 2022 General Elections in Kenya saw a dramatic increase in GBV (including TFGBV), and as the 2027 General Elections in Kenya approach, this project is timely and needed to support inclusive online civic engagement and to support the prevention of TFGBV amongst marginalised communities.Targeting informal settlements in Nairobi, Kiambu, Machakos, and Kajiado counties, this project will directly support communities most at risk and vulnerable to digital abuse in the lead up to the 2027 Elections, and learnings from this project can be shared with the Embassy’s other partners working on youth and women civic engagement.

title: Vodacom Group — Safaricom controlling stake, 2025
description:
"Pan-African telecoms operator Vodacom Group has announced a $2.1 billion deal that will see it increase its stake in Kenya's Safaricom to 55%. Under the terms of the deal, Vodacom has entered into an agreement with the Government of Kenya to acquire 15% of Safaricom PLC and an additional 5% from Vodafone at 34 Kenyan shillings (US$0.26) per share, valuing the deal at $2.1 billion." The transaction requires regulatory and governmental approvals in Kenya, Ethiopia and South Africa; Kenya retains a 20% stake and board representation.

Recipient countries: KEN, ETH.

title: Airtel Africa (Nxtra) — Kenya 44MW data centre, Tatu City, 2025
description: "India's Airtel has broken ground on a 44MW data center in Kenya, developed by Airtel Africa and its data-center arm Nxtra, located in Tatu City — a special economic zone outside Nairobi... The facility will be developed in two phases (22MW each), operational by Q1 2027 — reportedly the country's largest by capacity, with ~KES 19 billion (~$147 million) invested. Nxtra launched in Africa in January 2024 and is jointly owned by Airtel Africa and Carlyle (24% stake)."

title: Enhancing Digital Access and Community Resilience (EDACR) — Kenya ASAL Counties
description: Promotes digital inclusion and strengthens community resilience in eight Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASAL) counties in Kenya, including two refugee-hosting counties (Garissa and Turkana). Equips beneficiaries with digital literacy skills and access to digital financial services. Two parallel activities: -403 covers refugee-hosting counties (Garissa, Turkana, £1M); -404 covers wider eight ASAL counties (Wajir, Mandera, Garissa, Tana River, Samburu, Turkana, Marsabit, Isiolo, £1.3M). Both started August-October 2025, completing March 2026.

description: In 2017, Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.  and the Government of Kenya’s Ministry of Information, Communication and Technology (ICT) proposed the Konza Data Centre and and Smart City Project as part of a larger Konza Technology City (also called Konza Technopolis) initiative. Then, on April 26, 2019, China Eximbank and the Government of Kenya's Ministry of Finance signed an RMB 1,225,000,000 (Ksh 17 billion) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement for the Konza Data Centre and and Smart City Project. The proceeds of the loan are to be used by the borrower to finance a commercial contract with Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd, which was signed on June 22, 2017.   The lender made disbursements worth RMB 90,653,760.44 between July 1, 2019 and June 30, 2020 (Fiscal Year 2019-2020), RMB 131,870,086.70 between July 1, 2020 and June 30, 2021 (Fiscal Year 2020-2021) and RMB 247,718,790.85 between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2022 (Fiscal Year 2021-2022).  The loan’s amount outstanding was RMB 90,653,760.44 as of June 30, 2019, RMB 222,523,847.14 as of June 30, 2020, RMB 354,393,933.84 as of June 30, 2021, and RMB 602,112,724.69 as of June 30, 2022.   The purpose of the project is to construct a National Cloud Data Center, Smart ICT Network, Public Safe City and Smart Traffic Solutions, and a Government Cloud and Enterprise Service. The project site is located approximately 61 km from Nairobi, 51 km from Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA), and 400 km from Mombasa. title: Kenya Statistics Program for Results
description: The development objective of the Statistics Program (SP)-for-Results Project for Kenya is to support the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS) to generate better and more accessible data to inform policy-makers and contribute to strengthening its capacity. Progress towards the program development objective (PDO) will be monitored through four PDO-level indicators which, together, provide a coherent framework to measure increased capacity of KNBS to generate better and more accessible data to inform policy-making. The program results framework and disbursement linked indicator (DLIs) are built on the KNBS SP foundations and organized along the four intermediate results areas (IRA) which provide a logical results chain towards achieving the PDO. The results-oriented KNBS SP 2013-17 is framed around six strategic pillars and aims to address the above challenges. The 2013-17 SP was endorsed by the KNBS Board in December 2014 and is organized around six strategic focus areas: (1) addressing data gaps; (2) improving the quality of statistical information; (3) mainstreaming statistics in ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs), and county governments; (4) expanding communication, dissemination, and access to statistical information; (5) strengthening human resource management; and (6) undertaking institutional reforms and good governance.
